title: Fear, belief and approaching a stranger
header_line: My analysis of one book on negotiation. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What belief stops you from walking up to a person?

I said that if you see a famous chief executive at a dinner and he tells you to go talk to them, you may say you cannot, and the reason is a chain: a trigger, then a belief such as I am not good enough, then a lack of confidence.
I said that this is not in the book, that they are studying negative language patterns and belief systems, and that fear is revealing.
I said that what is relevant is not to have that fear, because it will not help you.
I said that you praise the process, but if you are being rejected every day you may start to blame the product, the service and the market. I called that the blame game.
I said that the first thing I think of in an entrepreneur is achievement, and that some people say he is just born like that, which is a method to the madness.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the person you would like to approach.
Write the belief that stops you.
Write the sentence to replace it.

choices: A trigger, a belief, a lack of confidence
A plan, a price, a profit
A call, a meeting, a deal

check.q: What did I say fear does?

recap: Trigger, belief, action. Replace the belief.
